clue.text: Like an early spinning wheel, inexhaustible?

definitions.meaning: an early wheel had no rubber tyre round its rim, spelt 'tire' in older usage, so it was without a tire

explanation.surface: Someone praises an old-fashioned spinning wheel as able to keep turning forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tire' is the older spelling of tyre: an early wheel had bare wood or iron with no rubber rim.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never wears out or runs dry is untiring, which is the second sense; the first splits the word as tire-less.

clue.text: Of the clans, some' think roast rib a luxury

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: A remark on taste: certain people consider roast rib of beef an indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Clans are tribes, so something belonging to a clan is tribal.

clue.text: Floors are often so' rough

definitions.meaning: floors are often covered with rugs

explanation.surface: Floors are often uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor laid with rugs is rug-ged; rough craggy ground is rugged too.

clue.text: See articles to detest

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone looks over some contracts and comes to hate them.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to hate it intensely.

clue.text: Lay emphasis on Miss Nightingale?

parts.note: a lay is a short song or ballad
emphasis is stress

explanation.surface: A tribute that dwells on the merits of Florence Nightingale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Nightingale' suggests Florence the nurse, but here it is a female singer, a nightingale being a sweet songbird; 'on' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with a fine voice is called a nightingale, after the songbird, so she is a female singer.

clue.text: Scotsman shows hesitation and gets a duck

parts.note: a Scotsman is a Scot
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A Scotsman stammers and then picks up a duck, perhaps for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts.

clue.text: Muse of fair melodies

definitions.meaning: one of the nine Muses, patron of epic poetry
a steam organ playing tunes at fairgrounds and circuses

explanation.surface: A goddess inspires beautiful songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Greek Muse of epic poetry, and the same name belongs to a steam whistle organ heard at fairgrounds.

clue.text: Alphonse's hero shows a pair of sailors in

indicators.note: the word for a sailor appears twice in a row

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's champion turns up flanked by two seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: Alphonse Daudet wrote the comic novel Tartarin de Tarascon about a boastful hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: Daudet's comic novels centre on the boastful Provençal Tartarin, his title character.

clue.text: Bits of blood found in Moscow gaol ?

definitions.meaning: cells in a Communist prison, red being the Soviet colour

explanation.surface: Fragments of blood are discovered in a Russian prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Erythrocytes are the corpuscles that carry oxygen; cells of a Soviet jail would be Communist, hence red, cells.

clue.text: Dyes deeply but in smallest quantities

parts.note: a grain is the smallest unit of weight, so grains are the tiniest amounts

explanation.surface: Something colours a fabric thoroughly while using only the tiniest amounts of dye.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingrain is to work colour deep into the fibre, so the verb means dyeing something thoroughly.

clue.text: Like the skirt that went up in flames?

definitions.meaning: a ... skirt widens out towards the hem
burst into sudden fire, blazed up

explanation.surface: A skirt caught fire and blazed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt cut to widen at the hem is described as flared; a fire that suddenly blazed has flared.

clue.text: Nymph and Spring are thus a single entity

indicators.note: the three words are run together as one unit, so their letters read as a single word

explanation.surface: A philosophical claim that a nymph and a spring are really one and the same being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single entity' tells you to run 'are thus a' together as one word. In Greek myth the nymph Arethusa was turned into a spring, which is why the definition names both.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Arethusa was a nymph whom Artemis turned into a freshwater spring in Sicily.

clue.text: He's mainly occupied with illegal takeovers

definitions.text: He's mainly occupied with illegal takeovers

parts.words: He's mainly occupied with illegal takeovers
parts.note: read 'mainly' as 'on the main', the open sea, where this outlaw seizes ships unlawfully

explanation.surface: A corporate raider who spends most of his time on shady business acquisitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' looks like 'chiefly' but means 'on the main', the old word for the high seas, where ships are seized.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea robber spends his life on the ocean seizing other vessels by force, an unlawful takeover.

clue.text: Crosses the line between denominations'

parts.note: inter is a Latin prefix meaning between
religious denominations are sects

explanation.surface: Someone oversteps the boundary separating religious groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or paths that cut across one another meet and cross at a point.

clue.text: Put plainer before marriage

annotationWithheld.why: Put plainer before marriage (10): PRENUPTIAL is an anagram of all of 'Put plainer' with no other anagram indicator, so 'Put' would have to be both fodder and indicator

clue.text: Drops the disguise with smashing result

indicators.note: the letters are given a disguise by being put into another order

explanation.surface: Someone throws off a disguise and the effect is spectacular.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken fragment of pottery is what remains after a pot is smashed.

clue.text: Whither hence in the cinema ?

parts.note: 'where to from here?' answered by a film title, From Here to ...

explanation.definitionFit: The 1953 film From Here to Eternity names where one goes from here.

clue.text: Perhaps this untidy creature is last to get the bird

indicators.note: the word last may be rearranged, a hint of perhaps another order

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An untidy animal is the last to be given the bird, maybe at a feeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' at the far end signals the rearrangement of 'last' into SLAT; 'to get' joins it to TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is a slovenly, untidy woman.

clue.text: Beaten at the 'open-air school?

definitions.meaning: pupils whose lesson is held outdoors are ... together

explanation.surface: Someone was defeated at a school that teaches outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: OUT (in the open air) and CLASSED (put in a school class).
explanation.definitionFit: Being far surpassed by a rival means being beaten; the split OUT plus CLASSED describes a class taught outdoors.

clue.text: Plant to produce beer, about 4½ gallons

indicators.note: the beer's letters go around the word for the cask

parts.note: ale is beer
a pin is a small cask holding four and a half gallons

explanation.surface: Brew some beer from a plant, roughly a few gallons' worth.
explanation.walkthrough: A pin is an old cask measure, half a firkin, holding four and a half gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine is a plant native to high mountain slopes, often grown in rock gardens.

clue.text: " Sessions of sweet —— thought " (Shakespeare)

parts.note: the opening of Shakespeare's Sonnet 30 with one word missing where the dash stands

explanation.definitionFit: Sonnet 30 begins 'When to the sessions of sweet silent thought', so the missing word is the quiet one.

clue.text: Standing in need of a' symbol ?

definitions.meaning: a ... symbol is a possession flaunted to show one's rank

explanation.surface: Someone stands waiting, wanting an emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: One's standing is one's rank in society; a status symbol is an object displaying that rank.

clue.text: Right in spite of -the fairy

indicators.note: the letter for 'right' is placed inside the word spite

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rightful claim persists despite opposition from the fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in spite of' looks like a single phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'spite' is the word being opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a small elf or other supernatural spirit of folklore.

clue.text: David or Bob in the 'grip of a fortune-teller

indicators.note: the shilling's letter is held inside the palm-reader's title

parts.note: a palmist tells fortunes by reading hands
a bob was a pre-decimal British shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: Either David or Bob has fallen into the clutches of a clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name beside David, but it is old British slang for a shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing many of the Psalms, so he is the psalm-writer.

clue.text: They are unwilling: to live abroad

definitions.text: They are unwilling: to live abroad

parts.words: They are unwilling: to live abroad
parts.note: people banished from their homeland who live in a foreign country against their wishes

explanation.definitionFit: People forced out of their own country by law or circumstance live overseas without choosing to.

clue.text: You can't mean it !

parts.note: something done without intent, which by its nature nobody means to do

explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is by definition unintended, so nobody can mean to cause one.

clue.text: Essential part of a smoking-cure

parts.note: curing meat or fish by smoke works by removing its moisture

explanation.definitionFit: Smoke-curing preserves food mainly by taking the water out of it, and a teetotal regime is also a way of going dry.

clue.text: Mineral suitable for firemen

definitions.meaning: fireproof suits for firefighters were once made of this material

explanation.surface: A mineral is recommended for use by fire crews.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a heat-resistant fibrous silicate once woven into protective clothing for fire crews.
